# --existing-only preflights the whole batch before pushing any branch.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-08-05T12:00:00Z'

cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'

shamhub-setup
shamhub new origin alice/example.git
shamhub register alice
git push origin main

env SHAMHUB_USERNAME=alice
gs auth login

# Create two tracked branches, but only publish the bottom branch.
git add first.txt
gs branch create first -m first
gs branch submit --fill

git add second.txt
gs branch create second -m second
gs branch submit --no-publish
stderr 'Pushed second'

# Advance both branches locally. The top branch remains unmapped.
gs branch checkout first
git add first-update.txt
gs commit create -m 'update first'
gs branch checkout second
gs branch restack
git add second-update.txt
gs commit create -m 'update second'

# The preflight must fail before updating the already-mapped bottom branch.
! gs stack submit --update-only --existing-only --fill
stderr 'branch "second" has no associated change request'

# The remote bottom branch still points to its original submitted commit.
git rev-parse origin/first
stdout '^b12ba7f8213768eeb2beb48575ac7e436d545028$'
git rev-parse first
! stdout '^b12ba7f8213768eeb2beb48575ac7e436d545028$'

shamhub dump changes
stdout '"ref": "first"'
stdout '"sha": "b12ba7f8213768eeb2beb48575ac7e436d545028"'

-- repo/first.txt --
first
-- repo/second.txt --
second
-- repo/first-update.txt --
first update
-- repo/second-update.txt --
second update
